shape: a place named in the text read as the project's own country
input: A World Bank tender whose location field says exactly 'Georgia'. Also the bare strings Austin, Fiji, Malawi, Chad, Zambia, Bronx and 'Gambia, The'.
assertion: resolveGeography returns the country the place is in. 'Georgia' alone is the country, not the US state; 'Austin' is not Australia; Fiji, Malawi, Chad, Zambia and Gambia are themselves; Bronx is New York City. And every genuine code string still resolves: CZ010/CZE, ROU, FIN, HUN/HU322, and the extra-regio HRZZZ.
origin: Third Regional Development Project - three World Bank tenders for museum work at Stepantsminda and Mtskheta, both in the Republic of Georgia - is filed under country=United States, region_state=Georgia. It therefore sits inside every US-scoped client scope, and client-scope.audit cannot see it because the composer and the database agree about the wrong country. Two separate branches produce this: the US-state scan runs before the sovereign-country list, and the NUTS code-like branch reads the first two letters of any 3-6 character place as an ISO-2 code (Austin -> AU -> Australia, Fiji -> FI -> Finland, Malawi -> MA -> Morocco, Chad -> CH -> Switzerland). The second is the Bronx -> Brazil defect, whose fix covered only configured jurisdictions. CLOSED 2026-08-18. The branch was parts.every(codeLike), the legacy TED path, which fires on a single-word place name because one word trivially satisfies every. The old pattern accepted Austin, Fiji, Chad, Zambia, Malawi, Gambia, Queens and Bronx as codes and REJECTED the two-letter ISO2 codes it existed for. Fixed by making the shape of a real code explicit - ISO2, ISO3, or two letters plus a digit-bearing suffix, plus the literal ZZZ extra-regio marker - and by consulting the country-name table before the code table. Measured: 4 live projects and 26 live records change country; 3 records lose one, of which 2 are the Austin fix.

shape: a headline with no filing behind it, from a place we do not cover

assertion: inCorpusScope refuses a resolved foreign country, admits the United States, and ADMITS null. An unresolved country is not a foreign one: 104 live press records resolve to no country and they include Fort Wayne and Brandywine Zoo, so failing closed on unknown would discard US coverage to enforce a rule about foreign coverage.
origin: 216 of 451 live press records had resolved outside the United States - Saudi Arabia 40, Australia 36, the UAE 33 - with no adapter pointed at any of them, so each was a headline with no filing behind it. 212 were tombstoned; 4 were held back because their own text says Austin, Texas or United States and the resolver disagreed, which is the 1H defect.

shape: a number attached to the wrong project, or to no sentence at all
input: An article body carrying '752 rooms' in a sentence naming Kulik River, and 'US$20 billion' in a sentence about the Strip generally. Plus a fact list holding a display string absent from the body.
assertion: extractPressFacts returns only figures printed in the text, each with the sentence it came from; verifyNoInvention THROWS on a display string not present in the body; and factsForEntry keeps the attributed figure and drops the one whose sentence never names the project.
origin: Reading 11 articles about Heart Hotel produced 73 figures, of which 66 were about other developments: Las Vegas round-ups name the project in one paragraph and four others in the rest. Every one of those numbers was correctly read out of real text, which is what makes it dangerous - nothing about 'US$20 billion' looks wrong in a document until a reader who knows the project sees it. Attribution on single name tokens was not enough either: 'capital', 'heart' and 'anaheim' matched ordinary English and city names, so single tokens now have to identify.

shape: a number attached to a quotation that does not contain it
input: An article whose first unbroken run is longer than the 400-character sentence cap, with the figure past the cut - the OCVIBE press release opening "Back To News Press Releases Press Releases OCVIBE and Award-Winning Art and Design Studio, FUTUREFORMS, Unveil...", with "100-acre" beyond character 400.
assertion: sentenceFor caps AROUND the match rather than from the front, so every fact returned by extractPressFacts satisfies fact.sentence.includes(fact.display); and verifyNoInvention THROWS on a fact whose sentence does not contain its own display, not only on one absent from the body.
origin: The sentence cap was .slice(0, 400) from the START of the sentence, so a figure late in a long run was stored with a quotation that does not contain it. verifyNoInvention passed it because it checks the display against the ARTICLE BODY, where the number genuinely is - the right question asked of the wrong text. It surfaced only at the document boundary, where the report provenance gate refused to render the figure and failed generation of the whole August report. Three guards now: the cap is taken around the match, verifyNoInvention checks the sentence as well as the body, and report-entry drops an unquotable figure so one bad stored row cannot take out every document.

shape: a label that names who presented a matter, read as who is behind it
input: A Clark County Redevelopment Agency agenda sheet whose only labelled name is 'PETITIONER: Denis Cederburg, Director of Public Works', and a zoning agenda sheet carrying a real 'APPLICANT:' alongside a petitioner.
assertion: contactsFromText puts a PETITIONER value in presented_by and NEVER in applicant; a document whose only labelled name is a petitioner yields applicant null; and a document that also names an APPLICANT keeps the applicant and does not let the petitioner overwrite it.
origin: PETITIONER sat in OWNER_LABELS, so Clark County's word for the officer who BRINGS an item to the Board was read as the party behind the project. Seven records stored a county officer as the applicant and five reached a live project: Lisa Kremer, Deputy County Manager on 215 And Windmill Lane; Anna Danchik, Comptroller on the transportation bonds project; Jennifer Ammennan, Deputy Director of Comprehensive Planning on BDA South; Denis Cederburg, Director of Public Works on 163 At Casino Drive. Each printed as '[RECORD] <officer> - applicant' with a link to a county document. SAME SHAPE AS ROADMAP 1I, the Legistar sponsors finding: a sponsor answers who in government moved this item and never who is behind this project, and every one of the 24 sponsors in the corpus is an elected official or a department. Measured before the change: all 7 records the label produced are county officers and not one is a real applicant, so moving it costs nothing that was ever right.

shape: a heading detector that fires inside the text it is dividing

assertion: readFilingFacts groups each condition under the department heading it sits below, splits a heading off the tail of a wrapped bullet, and does NOT split a condition on a department name used inside its own sentence. Every fact survives verifyFilingFacts.
origin: Clark agenda sheets wrap mid-clause at about 90 characters, so a department heading arrives glued to the previous bullet and a generic Title Case heading rule cannot see it. Detecting headings from a closed list fixed that and immediately caused the opposite defect: "Applicant to coordinate with Public Works - Development Review for all driveways" was cut to "Applicant to coordinate with" and opened a phantom group. A heading is always followed by the first bullet of its own list; a mention inside a sentence never is, which is what the rule now requires. Measured before and after: 140 conditions across 13 of 18 agenda sheets, 7 departments, and one truncated condition before the fix and none after.

shape: a boundary list missing one entry, read as the field being absent

A newline-separated ZAP record reading "CEQR number: 23DME005Q
CEQR type: Type I
CEQR lead agency: DME
Actions: ZS", where CEQR lead agency is the label that must close the CEQR type value.
assertion: readNycFacts returns nyc_ceqr_type for a record that carries the label, and its display is the value alone rather than the value plus the head of the next label.
origin: CEQR lead agency was missing from the next-label lookahead. In real newline-separated raw_content the value pattern cannot cross into the next field, so the lookahead is the only way a match can close, and with the next label absent the field read as NOTHING: 92 ZAP records carry CEQR type and 1 stored it. It survived the vocabulary pass, which counts Label: occurrences and never runs the reader, and it survived a synthetic single-line test, where with spaces instead of newlines the value runs on and closes at a later label - swallowing CEQR but still matching. It was caught only by printing the stored per-field rate against the measured one in the same run, which is why capture:filings prints that comparison.

The provenance gate had passed; the membership gate had never run. A read-back tool that builds a different document from the composer is worse than none, because it is trusted - and the read-back skill exists precisely to catch what the suite cannot.
